articles.title: IBM to stop US visa, green card sponsorship for majority of Consulting jobs
articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: IBM will no longer sponsor US visas or green cards for most of its consulting roles, citing increased regulatory scrutiny on foreign labor.
articles.explain: Visa sponsorship is when a company takes on the legal and financial responsibility to help a foreign worker obtain the legal right to work in the US. By stopping this for consulting jobs, IBM is signaling that it will prioritize local US-based talent, likely to avoid legal compliance costs and align with tightening federal regulations on immigration.

story.title: IBM Curbs Foreign Worker Sponsorship
story.so_far: Large technology and consulting firms have historically relied on H-1B visas and similar programs to recruit specialized technical talent globally. Recent years have seen shifting US immigration policies and increased scrutiny from Washington regarding the hiring of foreign workers in high-tech industries, prompting companies to adjust their recruitment pipelines.

timeline.text: IBM announced a shift in its hiring policy for consulting positions, ending visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of these roles.

articles.title: Global cotton output to decline as US, India crops shrink, says USDA
articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: The USDA projects a decline in global cotton production due to smaller crop yields in the US and India.
articles.explain: The USDA (US Department of Agriculture) tracks global crop data to help markets predict future supply and demand. A 'decline in output' means less cotton will be available on the global market. Because demand for cotton remains steady for clothing, a supply shortage generally leads to higher prices for textile manufacturers and potentially consumers.

story.title: Global Cotton Supply Outlook
story.so_far: Cotton is a vital commodity for the global textile and apparel industry. Production levels are highly sensitive to weather patterns, geopolitical stability, and trade policies. India and the US have long been two of the world's largest producers, and their agricultural performance directly affects global prices for clothing manufacturers.

timeline.text: New data from the USDA indicates that lower cotton output in major producing nations like India, the US, and Turkey will outweigh production gains in China and Australia.

articles.title: India and France deepen space cooperation, launch critical technologies dialogue
articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: India and France have initiated a new dialogue focused on critical technologies and space cooperation.
articles.explain: A 'critical technologies dialogue' is a formal diplomatic process where countries align on how to develop and secure essential industries like computing, space exploration, and defense. By working together, India and France aim to become less dependent on third-party suppliers for the hardware and software required to run their economies and militaries.

story.title: India-France Technology Partnership
story.so_far: India and France have historically maintained strong strategic partnerships in defense and aerospace. As global competition in semiconductor, AI, and space sectors intensifies, both nations are looking to diversify their technological dependencies away from other dominant global powers.

timeline.text: The two nations are deepening industrial and strategic ties through a new critical technologies dialogue aimed at improving supply chain resilience.

articles.title: Iran’s economic pain to intensify in coming months, says Marco Rubio
articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: Senator Marco Rubio suggested that Iran will face worsening economic conditions due to tougher US policies.
articles.explain: An 'economic pressure campaign' usually involves sanctions—government-imposed trade restrictions—that make it difficult for a country to sell its natural resources or access international banking. If Iran's economy is squeezed, global oil prices often rise because the market anticipates supply disruptions in key shipping regions like the Strait of Hormuz.

story.title: Strait of Hormuz Geopolitical Tensions
story.so_far: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime chokepoint for global oil. Tensions involving Iran, the US, and other regional powers often fluctuate based on sanctions and military posture. These tensions directly influence global energy prices and international diplomatic stability.

timeline.text: Regional actors have issued threats to close the Strait of Hormuz unless specific conditions are met by the US government.
Diplomatic efforts between Iran and Qatar are providing temporary relief to oil markets, causing prices to slide.

articles.title: Fossil CEO says turnaround is ahead of plan as sales return to growth
articles.summary: Watchmaker Fossil reports that its turnaround plan is yielding results, with a return to both profit and sales growth.
articles.explain: A 'turnaround' is a corporate recovery plan for a struggling business. When a company reports a 'return to profit,' it means it is finally making more money from sales than it is spending on operations. For Fossil, this suggests their new strategy—possibly focusing on different designs or reducing costs—is starting to work after a period of financial decline.

story.title: Fossil Group Turnaround Progress
story.so_far: Fossil Group, known for its watches and accessories, has struggled in recent years as consumer preference shifted toward smartwatches and away from traditional timepieces. The company has been closing underperforming stores and adjusting its product lineup to stabilize finances.

timeline.text: Fossil confirms its first signs of profitability and growth as the company executes its restructuring strategy.

articles.title: Anthropic targets $90 billion IPO at $1.4 trillion valuation
articles.summary: AI company Anthropic has officially initiated its IPO process, targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion and aiming to raise over $90 billion.
articles.explain: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time to raise capital. Anthropic is seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation, which would make it one of the most valuable companies in the world. Investors are watching this closely as a barometer for the broader AI industry's actual commercial potential versus its hype.

story.title: Anthropic Massive IPO Launch
story.so_far: Anthropic is a prominent artificial intelligence research company known for its Claude AI models. It is a major competitor to OpenAI and has attracted significant backing from tech giants like Amazon and Google. The company is now pursuing one of the largest public market debuts in history, reflecting the massive capital influx into the AI sector.

timeline.text: The company has defined its pricing range of $70-$78, aiming to raise $64.35 billion through the issuance of 825 million shares.
Anthropic has set a target valuation of $1.4 trillion and plans to begin trading on the Nasdaq on November 19.

articles.title: Wall St retreats as hot inflation data, Fed comments fuel rate worries
articles.summary: U.S. stock markets declined following reports of persistent inflation and cautionary comments from Federal Reserve officials.
articles.explain: When inflation data is 'hot,' it means prices are rising faster than expected, which often forces the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates high to cool the economy. High interest rates make it more expensive for companies to borrow money and reduce the 'present value' of future earnings, which tends to hurt stock prices, especially for tech firms.

story.title: US Tech Market Volatility
story.so_far: The US tech market has faced a turbulent 2026 as high interest rates and changing advertising demand have pressured growth-focused digital and software companies. Many of these firms saw inflated valuations during the previous cycle and are now undergoing significant market correction.

articles.title: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures
articles.summary: Major crypto firms including Coinbase and Kalshi have filed legal support for the CFTC regarding the regulation of stock-based perpetual futures.
articles.explain: The CFTC is a U.S. government agency that regulates the futures and options markets. 'Perpetual futures' are a type of derivative that allows traders to hold a position indefinitely without the contract expiring. The industry wants the right to offer these on stocks, while regulators are cautious about the risk and jurisdictional oversight required to keep these markets safe.

story.title: Regulation of Stock Perpetuals
story.so_far: The crypto industry has been pushing to expand the types of products available on regulated exchanges. Perpetual futures are complex derivatives that allow traders to bet on the price movement of an asset without an expiration date. There is ongoing conflict between federal regulators and exchanges over who has the authority to approve these types of speculative financial products.

timeline.text: Crypto entities are backing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a legal battle to permit trading of perpetual futures tied to individual stocks.
Additional crypto firms have joined the effort to support the CFTC in the ongoing legal dispute regarding stock-based perpetual derivatives.

articles.title: Coinbase, Kalshi, Kraken parent back CFTC in legal fight over stock perpetual futures
articles.summary: Kraken joined Coinbase and other industry players in a collective legal filing supporting the CFTC's stance on perpetual stock futures.
articles.explain: By backing the regulator (the CFTC), these exchanges are trying to gain legal clarity that would allow them to offer new, high-risk investment products. These firms argue that allowing these trades on regulated platforms provides transparency, whereas current restrictions might push this volume to less-regulated or offshore markets.

articles.title: Securitize agrees to buy River One to expand into asset-backed lending
articles.summary: Securitize is acquiring River One to integrate stablecoin funding into the asset-backed lending market. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
articles.explain: Asset-backed lending involves loans secured by tangible collateral, like equipment or inventory. By using stablecoins—cryptocurrencies pegged to the value of a fiat currency like the US dollar—Securitize aims to make this type of lending faster and more accessible. This matters as it represents a growing trend of institutional financial players adopting blockchain to streamline traditional credit markets.

articles.title: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic
articles.summary: North Korean hackers are launching new memecoins to launder funds stolen from a $6.3 billion Binance hack.
articles.explain: A 'memecoin' is a cryptocurrency inspired by internet memes, often lacking traditional utility. In this context, hackers create them as a cover to move money through 'liquidity pools'—decentralized pools of funds—to make it difficult for authorities to track the stolen money back to its source.

story.title: North Korean Crypto Laundering Tactics
story.so_far: North Korean state-sponsored hackers are widely recognized by international intelligence as being responsible for multiple large-scale cryptocurrency exchange breaches. By moving funds through various chains and decentralized protocols, they attempt to bypass global financial sanctions and convert stolen digital assets into usable currency.

timeline.text: Blockchain firm Elliptic discovered hackers using new tokens on the NEAR blockchain to obscure the flow of stolen assets.
Multiple reports confirm the use of memecoins to launder billions in stolen crypto assets.
